solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shock vote for way to trap Conservative

parts.note: to elect is to vote someone into office

indicators.note: to trap is to hold something caught inside, so one letter sits within the road word

parts.note: a route is a way to go

explanation.surface: An outrageous ballot plan to snare a Tory politician is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill or injure with an electric current is to deliver a fatal electric jolt, a literal sense of the verb.

clue.text: Man with inexhaustible bird?

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, and one that never runs out is a sentence for the rest of one's days

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a man with a tireless pet; 'bird' is British slang for time in prison (from rhyming slang 'bird lime' = time).
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a whole-of-life sentence has a stretch inside that never ends.

clue.text: Acquire backing in centre for procession

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed piece goes inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for acquire is read in reverse

parts.note: to acquire something is to get it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to gain support at the heart of a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral procession of mourners and cars is the usual sense of this French-derived word.

clue.text: Possibly metal case of Exocet missile

parts.note: heavy metal is one kind of rock music, so 'possibly' marks metal as an example of the broader genre

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Perhaps a metal casing for an Exocet guided missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes E and T, the outer letters of Exocet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is a self-propelled projectile weapon, a direct synonym for a missile.

clue.text: Caught out catching exhaust in raised road

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: someone who is out is away from home
to exhaust supplies is to use them up

explanation.surface: Someone caught out wandering is trapped by car fumes on an elevated road.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a road or track built up on an embankment across marshy ground or water.

clue.text: Scraps bird pecked on top of sill

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit, the past tense of bite, is what a beak does when it pecks

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird pecks at crumbs left on a windowsill.
explanation.definitionFit: Small tasty morsels of food or gossip are both scraps in the sense of little pieces.

clue.text: Free permit only came about without sweetheart once

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around into a new order
without says some letters of the fodder must be left out of the result

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A free pass came round only after a lover dropped out long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: PERMITONLYCAME has fourteen letters; rearranged 'about' it gives the answer once one E, the heart of 'sweet', is taken out ('without'). 'once' is a link meaning just one such letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Complimentary tickets are given free of charge as a courtesy, so the word is a synonym for gratis.

clue.text: Party with people present

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a nation is a people united by country

explanation.surface: A party attended by everyone in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift given to a cause, and a present is a gift.

clue.text: Cretins with no idea turning rude

indicators.note: turning means the letters are turned about into another order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Ignorant fools who have no clue become impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thoughtless of others' feelings is a form of rudeness, so the two adjectives are near synonyms.

clue.text: Tender chest, topless

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, so the first letter of the chest word is dropped

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: A sore chest belongs to someone going without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective meaning sore; it is the verb or noun sense of making a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender a bid or payment is to put it forward, the same as proposing it.

clue.text: Quiz show preceding 'The Ascent of Man'?

definitions.meaning: a long-running British TV word-and-numbers game show
before a rocket carries an astronaut upward, the seconds are called off from ten to zero

explanation.surface: A television quiz is scheduled before a documentary series on human history.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ascent of Man was a famous BBC documentary series, which makes this look like TV listings; read literally it is a crewed rocket launch.
explanation.definitionFit: The British game show of this name tests letters and numbers, and the same word names the count to zero before a launch.

clue.text: Struggle on exercise about to cover cut

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so the word for about goes around the next word

parts.note: re is Latin for about, regarding
to sever is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going with workouts despite a wound needing a dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, which is to struggle on.

clue.text: Avoid a homicide around American state

indicators.note: around here means the answer is found in the area of these words, sitting among them

explanation.surface: A warning to steer clear of a murder somewhere in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a western US state known for its potatoes.

clue.text: One periodical with endless bare pictures

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
mag is short for magazine, a periodical

indicators.note: a bare cupboard has nothing inside, so the word is emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: A single magazine filled with endless nude photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bare' empties 'endless' to its outer letters E and S; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are pictures or likenesses, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bound to have stake put on African runner

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one piece on another places it above, so the stake comes first

parts.note: an ante is a stake put into the pot in poker
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to bet on an African athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'obliged to'; Bound is the word for LOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The antelope is a fast-running hoofed animal of the African plains, playfully described as a runner.

clue.text: Runs batter over vegetables

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the whole joined string is read backwards

parts.note: spins are short drives or runs out in a car
to rap is to knock or batter

explanation.surface: Batsmen score runs and the bowler takes a beating over the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SPINSRAP into the answer; 'batter' looks like a cricketer or a cooking mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are pale root vegetables related to the carrot.

clue.text: Fool the woman employing one who makes dresses?

parts.note: a clot is a British word for a fool

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the word for one is taken inside

parts.note: her is the pronoun for the woman
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A foolish woman hires someone as her dressmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employing' puts I inside HER, making HIER. 'dresses' is a verb here: a clothier dresses people.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothier sells or makes clothes, so is someone who dresses customers, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Guts involves embracing redhead

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: to entail is to involve something as a consequence
the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: Courage is needed to hug someone with ginger hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' looks like courage in the surface; it means innards. 'embracing' puts R inside ENTAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the intestines or internal organs, the literal guts of an animal.

clue.text: Seemed a campus holds back university life

indicators.note: back means the contained letters are read backwards
holds means the words contain the answer's letters within them

explanation.surface: It seemed a college town was keeping students at bay from student life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' finds EMEDACA in 'seEMED A CAmpus' and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of universities and scholarship, academic life.

clue.text: High sound quality obtained by Sabbath died

indicators.note: obtained by means taken in by, so the outer letters hold the tone word

parts.note: d is short for died in records and family trees
tone is the quality of a sound

explanation.surface: A heavy metal band's high-pitched audio quality died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained by' puts TONE inside S and D; Black Sabbath, a heavy metal band, makes the surface musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for being high on drugs.

clue.text: Social networker's precious phrase cut short

parts.note: twee means affectedly dainty or precious

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the phrase word is lopped off

parts.note: a term is a word or phrase

explanation.surface: A social media user's prized saying has been abbreviated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes M off TERM, leaving TER; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who posts on Twitter is a user of a social network.

clue.text: Way to surmount enormous sadness

indicators.note: to surmount is to sit on top of, so in this down clue the way word comes above

parts.note: a path is a way
OS stands for outsize, enormous

explanation.surface: The road to overcoming great grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that evokes pity or sadness.

clue.text: Start to tour America taking in large city

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
taking in means holding inside, so the abbreviation for large goes within the country

parts.note: USA is the United States of America
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Kicking off a tour of the States with a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts L inside USA, giving ULSA after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a large city in Oklahoma.

clue.text: One touring time before composer left Queen

indicators.note: before means the time letter comes first in the string

parts.note: Ravel was a French composer, of Bolero fame
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A touring musician arrived before the composer abandoned the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is someone on a journey, one who tours.

clue.text: Sponge in a dessert rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a fool is a dessert of fruit purée and cream

explanation.surface: A sponge cake in a pudding is puffing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AFOOL upwards; 'Sponge' looks like a cake but is a bath sponge. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a bath sponge made from the dried fibre of a gourd.

clue.text: Top up Pilsner — he is drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Refill the lager glass, the man is tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to fill up again, the same as topping up.

clue.text: Hawk eating head of raw fish

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: to hawk goods is to tout them

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird of prey devours the head of an uncooked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird; it is the verb to sell. 'eating' puts R inside TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish.

clue.text: Mundane temporary head blunders penning English test

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so one letter sits inside

parts.note: errs means makes blunders
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A stand-in head teacher's mistakes are caught out by an English exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' puts E inside ERRS, giving ERRES after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Mundane in its older sense means of this world, earthly, as opposed to heavenly.
